name: cross-boundary-rail
prompt: the uprights are doing different work in these two. in the first they are all one thickness and the rail sits flat across them, which is why the run reads as plain; in the second every third one swells at the middle and the rail follows that swell--a third run made for this stair would have to decide whether the swell carries load or only announces itself

topic: two runs of ironwork read one at a time, where the one relation that matters is between them rather than inside either
why_this_fixture: HARNESS-003E's load-bearing frozen fixture. Every LOCAL batch succeeds and produces claims, and
the relation that matters connects two claims that were never in the same request: the sizing
puts the first run's atoms in one batch and the second run's in another, so no local call ever
Delete the cross-batch reconciliation and the local batches still go green. That is exactly the
failure a batched architect reports as a successful relation search, and it is why this fixture
asserts on the EDGE and the comparison claim rather than on the pass's outcome alone.
The same holds one pass along: the fork spanning the two batches survives in neither local
operationalization request, and `fork_payloads` is what the final cross-batch round found.
